readings.source: Front-month at ~€57.55/MWh on 28 Jul (per tradingeconomics.com/commodity/eu-natural-gas search snippet; direct page returned 403), up 1.52% on the day — easing back from the ~€59.39 four-month high of 21 Jul. Ongoing Hormuz disruption (Qatari tanker attack 7 Jul, Hormuz transits collapsed) continues to underpin elevated levels. Still within existing €57–60/MWh range; week-on-week direction has shifted from sharply rising to easing.

editorialReading: The hemisphere's fertilizer picture is stabilising this week after the Hormuz-driven spike, with prices consolidating rather than extending their gains. TTF front-month eased to ~€57.55/MWh on 28 July from last week's four-month high of ~€59.39 — a modest retreat that leaves the global nitrogen cost floor still materially elevated above any pre-crisis baseline. Urea has consolidated its recovery near ~$450–475/t (Egypt FOB Aug-26 futures ~$475/t), as the Egypt ad valorem duty release continues to be outweighed by the Hormuz war premium; the mid-July trough of ~$385–400/t now looks to have been the floor for this leg. The July Tampa ammonia contract — the Western Hemisphere's nitrogen benchmark — is confirmed at ~$800/t (up $25/t on June's $775/t); August settlement remains pending and will set the cost reference for the second-half US application season. Brazil continues buying potash at ~$405–415/t CFR granular, broadly unchanged, as Safrinha crop preparation advances. DAP holds near $755–760/st on the CME NOLA curve, supported by China's phosphate export restrictions running through August. The structural exposure for import-dependent Central American and Andean markets remains acute: the brief mid-July nitrogen-cost relief window has largely closed, and the second-half planting season faces sustained elevated input costs with the Hormuz disruption unresolved.
watchNext: Whether urea consolidates in the ~$450–475/t range or resumes its climb as the Hormuz premium resets market expectations; whether August Tampa ammonia settles above July's ~$800/t — the Western-Hemisphere benchmark for nitrogen input economics. Watch the CME DAP / urea curve for the US buy-side signal, Brazilian potash CFR into the Safrinha, and TTF gas as the global nitrogen cost floor. The squeeze on hemisphere food security runs less through US farmer prices than through import-dependent neighbours' access to affordable nitrogen. Sourcing note: real-time Argus / Green Markets assessments are subscription-only and the free World Bank Pink Sheet lags ~a month — these are publicly-cited indications.
